chunks: Indeed, obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is His service on the earth, and nothing from His service is equal to salat (prayer). For this reason, the angels called out to Zakariyya عليه السلام
"while he was standing, performing salat (prayer) in the sanctuary."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer, presented here as the highest act of service
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earthly realm where divine obedience is carried out
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who called out to Zakariyya عليه السلام
key_terms.خِدْمَتُهُ: serving Allah through devoted action on earth

ai.seo_question: Why is salat considered the greatest act of service to Allah in this hadith of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that obedience to Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ is realized through serving Him on earth, and that salat (prayer) is the greatest form of that service. It highlights the special rank of prayer by invoking the Qur'anic description of Zakariyya عليه السلام being called by the angels while he was engaged in worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.623 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Obedience to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, is to serve Him on earth, and there is nothing among His acts of service that equals prayer. This is why the angels called out to Zakariya (as)
'while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary' (Surah Ale ‘Imran 3:39)”.
